why: Film titles that contain a year later than the year they were released in. The anachronism check exists to catch a hallucinated future date, and a title is not a date, so each of these is an exemption from that check and has to be justified one at a time. Adding an entry means asserting that the string is a real title and that the year inside it is part of the name. The revue convention, where a 1935 page lists Broadway Melody of 1936, is handled generatively by the 'of YYYY' rule in validate-data.mjs and does not need entries here.
rules: The year inside the title must sit next to enough other text to be unmistakable. A film titled only with a bare number cannot be exempted this way, because the string is indistinguishable from a stray year, and one of those is exactly what the check is looking for. If such a title comes up, quote it in the year's notes and leave the check failing rather than widening this list to a bare number.
